title: End-to-End Processing Flow
html:
End-to-End Processing Flow

Complete pipeline from email ingest to the Excel posting file or exception handling.

1 · Email Ingest
2 · Classification
3 · Data Extraction
4 · BSID Lookup
5 · Match & Validate
6 · Confidence
7 · Decision
8 · Action

Key Terms — Definition & Evaluation

In-scope: AR-relevant remittance, Promise-to-Pay (PTP), or duplicate emails. Non-AR communications are treated as out-of-scope.

Duplicate: an email already processed or submitted multiple times; duplicate/reference evidence is evaluated using invoice/remittance references and supporting-reference checks.

Pending Review: records requiring human validation, typically where confidence is 40–79% or the match/evidence needs review.

Exception: a record with no SAP BSID match; it remains an exception regardless of confidence and requires investigation.

1. Email Ingest

Emails arrive in the monitored inbox. Each email is assigned a unique Entry ID and Email ID and timestamped for processing.

2. Classification

The AI engine classifies each email as:

  • Remittance — Payment remittance/advice emails containing invoice references and amounts
  • Promise to Pay (PTP) — Customer commitment to pay outstanding invoices on a specified date
  • Duplicate — Emails already processed or submitted multiple times
  • Out of Scope — Marketing, HR, sales, vendor invoices, or other non-AR emails

3. Data Extraction

For in-scope emails, the system extracts: Customer Name, Customer Number, Company Code, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, Remittance Reference, Amount, Currency, Payment Date, and attachment details (multi-attachment, body-only, credit note flags).

4. SAP BSID Lookup

The extracted invoice number is used to query the SAP BSID (Business Partner Sub-Item Document) table. The system attempts to match the invoice to an open AR item in SAP.

5. Match & Validate

The system validates: invoice number match level (EXACT / NEAR / NONE), amount alignment (within tolerance), currency match, customer name similarity, and date proximity.

6. Confidence Scoring

A weighted confidence score (0–100%) is computed from six components. Fast-path overrides can set the score directly for high-certainty scenarios.

7. Decision

  • ≥80% + BSID Match → Auto Process — Confirm & Extract to Excel / Change Details / Reject Record
  • ≥80% + No BSID Match → Exception — Add BSID Invoice Details / Confirm & Extract to Excel / Request Clarification / Reject Record
  • 40–79% → Manual Review — Add / Update Invoice Details / Confirm & Extract to Excel / Request Clarification / Reject Record
  • <40% → Manual Investigation — Add / Update Invoice Details / Confirm & Extract to Excel / Request Clarification / Escalate to AR Supervisor / Reject Record
  • Duplicate → Close as Duplicate / Request Clarification / Mark as Non-Duplicate / Add or Update Details
  • Out of Scope → Ignored

8. Action

Auto-processed records trigger a SAP BSID update. Manual review records are routed to the Collections Analyst queue. Exceptions are escalated to the AR Supervisor.

title: SAP BSID Validation
html:
SAP BSID Validation

How the system validates against the SAP Business Partner Sub-Item Document table.

What is BSID?

BSID is SAP's open AR item table. Each entry represents an outstanding invoice or credit note that a customer owes. The system queries BSID using the extracted invoice number to find a matching open item.

Match Criteria

  • Invoice Number: EXACT match with BSID XBLNR after normalisation (BELNR / VBELN accepted as alternates); NEAR (one OCR-confusable character) always goes to review
  • Customer Number: must match BSID_Customer_Number
  • Company Code: must match BSID_Company_Code
  • Currency: checked for alignment (currency mismatch = 0 on amount score)
  • Amount: within configured tolerance (default ±2%)

BSID Match Outcomes

BSID_Match_FlagBSID_Open_Item_StatusOutcome
1 (Yes)OpenAvailable for auto-processing
1 (Yes)Partially OpenAvailable, amount may differ
0 (No)—Exception / Investigation required

No BSID Match

If no BSID match is found, the record is flagged as an Exception regardless of confidence score. The exception reason is recorded as "No BSID match found" and the record is routed for investigation by the AR Supervisor.

Invoice / Reference Matching

Invoice-number matching and reference validation used as part of BSID validation.

Invoice Number Match

The extracted invoice number is compared with the BSID reference (XBLNR first; BELNR and VBELN are accepted when they match exactly). Both sides are normalised first: upper case, spaces and - / . removed, leading zeros removed.

Match levelInvoice Match ScoreRuleHandling
EXACT1.00Identical, or identical after normalisationNormal scoring; Fast Path eligible
NEAR0.70Exactly one character differs and it is a common OCR confusion (0/O, 1/I/L, 5/S, 8/B, 2/Z)Always Manual Review - "Possible OCR misread"
NONE0.00Anything elseException - "No BSID match found"

Remittance Reference

The Remittance Reference (e.g., REM-XXXXXX) is extracted as a secondary identifier. It is used in conjunction with invoice number for duplicate detection.

Exact Match Fast Path

An EXACT invoice-number match with an open BSID item, matching currency, and amount within ≤2% triggers the Fast Path (92%). If the amount is missing but all other criteria match, the score is set to 91%.

Amount, Currency, Customer & Date Validation

Additional validation checks applied to the candidate BSID item.

Amount Alignment

Amount Difference %Amount Alignment Score
≤2%1.00
2–5%0.80
5–10%0.60
10–20%0.30
>20%0.00
Amount missing0.00 (no penalty if fast path)
Currency mismatch0.00

Currency Validation

Currency must match BSID currency for a non-zero amount alignment score. A currency mismatch forces amount alignment to 0 regardless of the amount difference.

Customer Name Similarity

Fuzzy string similarity between extracted Customer Name and BSID_Customer_Name. Score range: 0.0–1.0. Exact match = 1.0, high similarity = 0.9+.

Date Proxy Score

Date Difference (days)Date Proxy Score
0–30 days1.00
31–90 days1.00
91–180 days0.60
>180 days0.20

Sender → Company Code Mapping

The sender domain is mapped against known customer-company code relationships. A confirmed match scores 1.0; no mapping scores 0.0.

title: Duplicate Detection
html:
Duplicate Detection

How the system identifies and handles duplicate submissions.

Duplicate Detection Logic

A record is flagged as a duplicate if it matches an existing record on all of the following:

  • Invoice Number (exact match)
  • Customer Number
  • Amount (within 0.01% tolerance)
  • Currency
  • Sender Email Domain
  • Submission date within 7 days of the original

Duplicate Reference

Each duplicate record stores a Duplicate_Reference_ID pointing to the original entry that was processed first. The duplicate is assigned status "Duplicate" and recommended action "Duplicate Review / Close as Duplicate".

Duplicate Handling

  • Duplicate records are excluded from core KPI calculations
  • They appear in the Action Queue with the Duplicate status badge
  • Analysts can review and close as duplicate or escalate if the original was processed incorrectly

title: Promise-to-Pay (PTP) Handling
html:
Promise-to-Pay (PTP) Handling

How the system processes customer payment commitments.

PTP Classification

An email is classified as PTP when the customer explicitly commits to paying on a specific date without providing an actual remittance. Key indicators include: "promise to pay", "will pay by", "payment commitment" in the subject or body.

PTP Processing Flow

  1. Email classified as "Promise to Pay"
  2. PTP_Flag and PTP_Intent_Flag set to 1
  3. Payment Date extracted from email content
  4. BSID lookup performed on referenced invoice numbers
  5. If BSID found: PTP logged, follow-up scheduled for Payment Date
  6. If no BSID: Exception raised for supervisor review

PTP vs Remittance

Unlike remittances, PTP records do not trigger immediate SAP updates. They are recorded as commitments and require follow-up validation once the payment date arrives.

PTP in the Dashboard

PTP records are included in the "PTP Intent" scenario card and shown with the orange PTP badge in all views. They are counted in Classification Distribution and included in accuracy calculations for in-scope records.

title: Out-of-Scope Handling
html:
Out-of-Scope Handling

Identifying and excluding irrelevant emails from AR processing.

Out-of-Scope Categories

CategoryExamples
Marketing communicationNewsletters, promotions, product announcements
Customer service querySupport tickets, complaints, inquiries
Sales inquiryRFQ, price requests, quote follow-ups
General correspondenceIntroductory emails, meeting requests
Vendor invoiceAP invoices mistakenly sent to AR mailbox
HR communicationEmployment queries, payroll questions
Bank notification unrelated to paymentBalance alerts, FX rate notifications

Impact on KPIs

  • Out-of-scope records are assigned Processing Status = "Ignored / Out of Scope"
  • They are excluded from core KPI calculations and accuracy metrics
  • The "Accuracy – Excl. Out-of-Scope" metric shows performance on truly relevant emails

title: Confidence Scoring Formula
html:
Confidence Scoring Formula

Complete specification of the five-component weighted confidence score.

Raw Score = (Invoice Match × 0.35) + (Amount Alignment × 0.30) +
(Sender→Company Code × 0.10) + (Customer Name × 0.05) +
(Date Proxy × 0.10)

Confidence Score = Raw Score ÷ 0.90 × 100%
ComponentWeightMax ContributionRange
Invoice Match Score0.35 (35%)0.350.0–1.0
Amount Alignment Score0.30 (30%)0.300.0–1.0
Sender→Company Code Mapping0.10 (10%)0.100.0 or 1.0
Customer Name Similarity0.05 (5%)0.050.0–1.0
Date Proxy Score0.10 (10%)0.100.0–1.0
Total Maximum Raw Score0.90

Note: The five weighted components total 0.90. Normalization maps the maximum raw score of 0.90 to 100%.

What Each Component Means

ComponentWhat it measuresWhy it matters
Invoice MatchHow many invoice/reference digits match the open BSID invoice number.Strong invoice-number evidence is the primary signal that the email refers to the correct open item.
Amount AlignmentHow closely the amount in the email matches the BSID amount, after currency validation.A close amount match reduces the risk of applying a remittance to the wrong invoice.
Sender → Company CodeWhether the sender/domain is associated with the company code on the candidate BSID item.Confirms that the email originated from a payer relationship expected for that company code.
Customer Name SimilaritySimilarity between the extracted customer name and the BSID customer name.Provides an independent customer-identity check when invoice references are incomplete or ambiguous.
Date ProxyHow close the relevant email/invoice date is to the BSID payment or posting date used by the model.Reasonable date proximity provides supporting evidence that the candidate transaction is the right one.

Fast-Path Rules

Override rules that set confidence directly for high-certainty scenarios.

Fast PathConditionsConfidence Score
EXACT match + full match EXACT invoice-number match + open BSID item + same currency + amount difference ≤2% 92%
EXACT match + amount missing EXACT invoice-number match + open BSID item + same currency + amount not available 91%

Confidence = max(fast-path value, formula). The formula is always calculated; the fast-path value wins only when it is higher, and it decides the category and decision. The Confidence Source field of a record says which one applied (FAST_PATH or FORMULA).

Thresholds & Decisions

Confidence ScoreCategoryBSID MatchDecisionAction
≥80%HighYesAuto ProcessConfirm & Extract to Excel; Change Details; Reject Record
≥80%HighNoExceptionAdd BSID Invoice Details; Confirm & Extract to Excel; Request Clarification; Reject Record
40–79%MediumYes/NoManual ReviewAdd / Update Invoice Details; Confirm & Extract to Excel; Request Clarification; Reject Record
<40%LowYes/NoManual InvestigationAdd / Update Invoice Details; Confirm & Extract to Excel; Request Clarification; Escalate to AR Supervisor; Reject Record
N/ADuplicateN/ADuplicateClose as Duplicate; Request Clarification; Mark as Non-Duplicate; Add or Update Details
N/AOut of ScopeN/AOut of ScopeIgnore

html:
Example Score Calculation

Step-by-step confidence score calculation for a sample record.

Input Data (ENT-000001)

FieldValue
Invoice Number (as written)23756669
BSID Invoice (XBLNR)23756668
Amount$13,497.36
BSID Amount$13,464.77
Currency / BSID CurrencyUSD / USD
Customer Similarity0.957 (Innova Care Products)
Date Difference144 days
Sender MappingConfirmed (1.0)

Component Scores - three cases

The same record, depending on how the invoice number reads. Amount (0.241% difference) scores 1.00 × 0.30 = 0.300, sender mapping 1.00 × 0.10 = 0.100, customer name 0.957 × 0.05 = 0.048, date proxy (144 days) 0.60 × 0.10 = 0.060 in every case.

Invoice number caseMatch levelInvoice Match (× 0.35)Raw ScoreConfidence (raw ÷ 0.90)Decision
As written: 23756669 vs 23756668 (9 vs 8 is not an OCR pair)NONE (0.00)0.0000.50856.4%Exception - No BSID match found
OCR variant: 2375666B (8 read as B)NEAR (0.70)0.2450.75383.7%Manual Review - Possible OCR misread (NEAR always goes to review)
Exact number: 23756668EXACT (1.00)0.3500.85895.3%Auto Process

Normalization & Decision (exact number)

Raw Score = 0.858 → ÷ 0.90 = 95.3% (formula)
Fast Path (EXACT + open BSID + same currency + amount within 2%) = 92%
Confidence = max(fast-path 92%, formula 95.3%) = 95.3% (source: FORMULA)
Confidence Category = High (≥80%) · BSID Match = Yes → Decision = Auto Process
Action = Confirm & Extract to Excel

The Fast Path can only raise a score, never lower it: here the formula is higher, so the formula value is used.
